nodes.summary: The Akari (Light Up) decision problem accepts a list of booleans $x$ exactly when $x$ decodes, under the canonical bitstring encoding of lists of lists of natural numbers, to an Akari board that is well formed and feasible; it rejects every list that does not decode.
nodes.title: The Akari decision problem

nodes.summary: Let $B$ be an Akari board with $m$ rows, let $n$ be the length of its first row ($n = 0$ when there are no rows), and write $B_{r,c}$ for the entry in row $r$ and column $c$, read as $1$ when there is no such entry. nodes.title: Feasible Akari boards

nodes.summary: An Akari instance is a board given as a list of rows, each row a list of natural numbers: the entry $0$ is an empty cell, $1$ is a wall, and $2 + k$ is a wall numbered $k$. The rows need not have the same length; that is part of well-formedness.
nodes.title: Akari boards

nodes.summary: The Akari decision problem belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: AKARI (LIGHT UP) is NP-complete

nodes.summary: Let $B$ be a board, a list of rows of natural numbers, and write $B_{r,c}$ for the entry in row $r$ and column $c$, read as $1$ when there is no such entry. A bulb at $(b_r, b_c)$ illuminates the cell $(r, c)$ when either $b_r = r$ and $B_{r,c'} = 0$ for every column $c'$ strictly between $b_c$ and $c$, or $b_c = c$ and $B_{r',c} = 0$ for every row $r'$ strictly between $b_r$ and $r$. nodes.title: Illumination on an Akari board

nodes.summary: An Akari board is well formed when every entry is at most $6$ and all its rows have the same length.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
